notes.text: The source continues a previous sentence. It says that the given orientations let one hold, for each edge a, a combinatorial polygon P_a with vertex set R_a, whose edge set can be described from R_a, omega_a, and the map to Circ(R_a). This claim is recorded as background without an independent proof.

It proposes recording the structure instead as a combinatorial contour: a set of rigidifying flags carrying an action of the displayed infinite dihedral group, together with a map to oriented edges compatible with the epsilon homomorphism to the signs. The displayed presentation uses braces and two involution relations, preserved as written.

The last subset is said to define an orientation of the corresponding contours. Its right-margin explanation identifies the free-edge part with gluing circles. The final boundary sign in the pi_0 formula remains doubtful, and the text literally omits an object between les and the membership sign; none has been supplied.
The source writes des contours correspondant, without a final s on the adjective, but uses plural recollements in the margin. Both visible endings are preserved.

The lower mark on R recurs as a short heavy or wavy underline. In the arrow display it ends in a pointed rightward flourish; comparison with the other occurrences supports keeping the same underline notation rather than adding a second vector accent.
The index written l is looped at each occurrence in the subset and margin note. C's l and H's ell are treated as typographical forms of the same letter, not a change of reading.
The page number is a current 7 over a doubtful cancelled 6. The pale folio 50 at the bottom is a separate numbering layer and is also transcribed.

Original image viewed once for layout; each prepared half viewed once line by line, including all witness agreements. Thirteen single evidence crops were created and viewed. No OCR, web, other-page files, or TeX compilation were used. The 31-line count includes the raised de, cancelled middle line, display rows, four marginal lines, and both number positions.
